The build process involves standard autotools steps: `autoreconf`, `automake`, `configure`, and `make`. These are expected operations for compiling C-based software from source. The package installs files into `$pkgdir` using `make install`, which is standard packaging behavior. No network requests, dynamic downloads, or suspicious commands (like `eval`, `curl|bash`, or obfuscated scripts) are present.

The package depends only on `fuse` and `libarchive`, both legitimate system libraries. The maintainer and contributors are credited normally. There is no evidence of malicious code injection, backdoors, or unauthorized system access. All operations align with standard AUR packaging practices for an open-source tool.
